response.rationale: The answers are semantically valid, but the national split is materially overstated. Indonesian pelit and Malaysian kedekut are plausible everyday preferences, yet Malaysian PRPM explicitly lists pelit, kikir, and lokek as accepted equivalents of kedekut; Indonesian lexicographic sources likewise connect pelit/kikir/lokek/kedekut. The relation should not imply a clean variety-exclusive contrast. No false-friend contrast is present or supported.
